beliefs: The cubic is nearly odd: f(-x)≈-f(x) for |x|>=2.6, e.g. f(-128)≈8175362 vs -f(128)≈8181913 [E1]
On the positive side f is smooth and monotone decreasing from about x=1.0 onward: f(1.0)≈1.7, f(1.5)≈-9.1, f(2.0)≈-25.3, f(2.6)≈-59.7 [E5]
The positive-side values at 0.9-1.1 are bumpy (f(0.9)≈0.92, f(1.0)≈1.70, f(1.1)≈0.89), so a small-|x| bumpy region exists roughly |x|<1.1 [E1, E5]
Near zero f is bumpy and non-monotone: f(0)≈3.02, f(±0.5)≈1.7-2.2, f(±0.9)≈0.9-4.8 [E1, E2, E5]
The negative side in [0.9,1.5] is irregular/noisy (f(-1.2)=6.61 in E4 vs 9.32 in E2, f(-0.9)=2.75 in E4 vs 3.81 in E2), unlike the smooth positive side [E2, E3, E4]
The special interval is roughly |x|<2.6 where f deviates from the cubic; the transition to cubic is near |x|≈2.6 [E3, E5]
The exact form inside |x|<2.6 is not pinned down; a smooth polynomial fit gives only approximate values there [E2, E3, E4, E5]?
notes: E5 shows the positive side is smooth and monotone from x=1.0 to 2.6, so I refit the near-zero polynomial using the new E5 points and kept the cubic threshold at 2.6, which the E5 endpoint f(2.6)=-59.7 confirms matches -3.9*x^3.
